headline: Search, Switched Off
thesis: Google's plan to make AI and Search off by default for K-12 student accounts has districts shopping for alternatives, as schools push vendors to disclose AI before they ship it.
summary: The day's biggest K-12 story is Google's plan to switch off its AI tools and Search by default for student accounts in early 2027: because AI is now built into Search, blocking one means losing the other. Large districts including New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago are reportedly weighing other search engines, and filtering vendors are adding AI Overview blocks. That fits a wider push on AI feature creep, with EdTech Magazine urging districts to inventory and risk-tier AI features that arrive inside tools they already approved. In higher ed, law school acceptance rates fell to a 20-year low as applications jumped 18%. 1EdTech's Learning Impact Award nominations close Nov. 23, and Ed-Fi's API v8.1 and 2027 roadmap continue to set the data-standards agenda.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · NOVEMBER 20, 2026 · Direct page fetches were blocked by this run's network policy, so items were gathered through web search; some sources had no new dated items and show recent evergreen content.
